title: Systematic physicochemical characterization, carbon balance and cost of production analyses of activated carbons derived from (Co)-HTC of coal discards and sewage sludge for hydrogen storage applications
material_description: AC-HCT | KOH-activated carbon from the hydrochar (HCT) of South African coal tailings (CT, coal beneficiation plant, Mpumalanga); HTC 150 °C, 27 bar, 95 min, solid concentration 0.25 g/mL; KOH:HC 4:1; ash 40.86 wt% (adb)
purification_method: washed with 0.5 N HCl, then distilled water (centrifuge) to pH ~6; dried at 60 °C in an oven for 24 h
activation_method: KOH chemical activation, KOH:HC weight ratio 4:1, tube furnace under N2 (150 mL/min), heating rate 15 °C/min; optimum 850 °C, 147.37 min (Table 3); text and Table 10 give 850 °C, 135 min
source_location: main text p. 141, Fig. 8a (77 K, cm3/g vs MPa) series "AC-HCT ads" (filled markers) and Fig. 9a (77 K, wt% vs P/P0) same series
notes: archive: HYC-0048_fig8a_AC-HCT_ads.json; archive: HYC-0048_fig9a_AC-HCT_ads.json. Fig. 8a: 0.44958 MPa (stored 4.49577 bar), 116.476 cm3/g; Fig. 9a: P/P0 0.1265, 3.462 wt%. Fig. 8 (cm3/g vs MPa) and Fig. 9 (wt% vs P/P0) plot the same measured points (paper: "volumetric and gravimetric measurement results ... are represented by Figs. 8 and 9"; every 77 K Fig. 9a abscissa = Fig. 8a pressure / 3.5 MPa, and cm3/g : wt% = 33.6 +/- 0.1 for every point), so each point is one row carrying both. Reported wt% disagrees with the cm3/g value beyond either convention (W1 from cm3(STP)/g is about 30% of the plotted wt%): unit-consistency failure; wt_pct_convention unknown. Fig. 8 axis is "Volume H2 (cm3/g)"; STP not stated, stored in uptake_ml_stp_g as the 0 °C/1 atm default. Occlusion: Fig. 8a marker partly hidden by another marker (30 px visible vs median 51); centroid of the visible part, possible bias up to ~3 px (<1% of axis span). Characterization (Table 6): BET 2021.91 m2/g (same in Tables 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 and text); total pore volume 1.77 cm3/g (Tables 5, 8, text; Table 3 gives 1.89, Table 4 1.88); BJH average pore diameter (4V/A) printed 36.6 Å, stored 3.66 nm (Tables 4 and 8 give 2.75 nm, method not stated); BJH adsorption surface area 1485.25 m2/g; skeletal (apparent) density by He pycnometer printed 2228.35 kg/m3, stored 2.22835 g/cm3. Composition (Table 6, wt%, air-dried basis): C 51.16, H 4.13, N 1.64, O 0.81, S 0.01; moisture 1.39, ash 40.86, volatile matter 6.81, fixed carbon 50.94; EDS shows C, O, Si, Fe. Basis not named by the paper; volumetric (Sieverts, Micromeritics HPVA) so basis_inferred = excess by instrumental default. Degassing: 373 K overnight in a vacuum system, then 373 K under vacuum for another 24 h in the HPVA 10 cm3 cell (degas_temperature_c from 373 K; duration = final 24 h stage); sample mass printed as "approximately 1.2 g"; H2 purity printed as grade "N5.0" (AFROX). Pore volume is Table 6 "BET adsorption total pore volume" (single-point N2, coded pore_volume_method = other). No BET P/P0 range stated in the text (Fig. 5b BET plot shows points over P/P0 ~0.05-1.0). Mineral matter (ash) not deliberately added; class kept activated_carbon.
free_volume_calibration: cold and warm (free) volume measured after the adsorption-desorption tests, "to avoid helium capture in narrow pores" (helium implied; gas and temperatures not stated)
